name: security-audit
works_with: Coding agents with tool use and parallel sub-agents
short: Cloudflare's skill that turns your coding agent into a security auditor that checks each finding twice.
what: A skill from Cloudflare that runs a security audit of a codebase in six phases: mapping the code, hunting for bugs, trying to disprove each candidate, writing structured findings, verifying them again with fresh agents, and writing a report. Every finding ends up as confirmed, needs validation, or rejected. Cloudflare says it's the single-repo starting point for its own vulnerability discovery harness.
who: Developers and security people who want a structured audit of their own code from their coding agent. If your agent can't run parallel sub-agents, this won't work as designed.
needs: A coding agent with a model that supports tool use and parallel sub-agents
Node.js, for the two small validator scripts the skill runs
An OS-enforced sandbox if you want it to build or run the target's code. Without one, it leaves those leads as needs validation

steps.title: Install the skill
steps.text: This uses the Skills CLI. Run `npx skills --help` to pick agents or install without prompts.

steps.title: Or install it for your user account
Start your agent in the code you want to audit
steps.text: Then ask for an audit. The skill switches on by itself when you ask for a security audit, a vulnerability hunt or a pen test.

try.label: From the README
try.where: Your coding agent, in the target repo
try.text:
security audit this codebase

Or:
find security vulnerabilities in ./src
do a security review, output to ~/audits/my-project

watch: A full audit starts many separate sub-agents for hunting and checking, and each one draws on your agent's plan or credits.
Reports go to `~/security-audit-skill/<repo-name>/run-<N>` unless you name a folder. It only writes inside the audited repo if you pick a folder that version control ignores.

The README's sandbox rules for running target code are strict: no outside network, a cleaned environment, resource limits and writes only to scratch folders. Don't let it run untrusted code outside one.
Runs add up. In Cloudflare's tests, one run found roughly half of what repeated runs found in total.
